batch_strategy: Select these 32 distinct supplied candidate IDs and freeze their supplied forecasts before measurement. Prioritize conditional model failures, informative loading contrasts, missing solvent-response points, and one targeted reproducibility check. Quantile spreads are secondary diagnostics from the single predictor.

choices.reason: Measure m125 in pure EA at 100 ul with a 300-ul DCM plug. Its measured 500-ul counterpart provides a direct contrast. The confirmed plug association at 1/1 makes this a useful test of transfer to stronger eluent.

This pure-EA m125 experiment at 50 ul and a 300-ul plug forms a matched plug contrast with the selected 500-ul experiment. Together with the selected 100-ul point, it tests amount-by-plug dependence where forecasts are nearly invariant.

Complete the pure-EA, 50-ul m125 plug contrast using 500 ul DCM. Existing 1/1 observations support a substantial completion association with plug volume; this pair tests its persistence without changing sample amount.

The observed table leaves m92 at 1/1, 150 ul and EA loading unmeasured. Its measured 50- and 100-ul endpoints differ substantially. This point distinguishes a continuing amount response from an isolated middle-amount elevation.

Measure m72 at 1/1 and 150 ul with DCM loading. Recent 100-ul DCM and PE loading packages gave similar endpoints. This point completes the DCM amount series and contrasts with the measured PE-loaded 150-ul condition.

Use this eligible repeat of m81 at 20/1 and 100 ul to test its recently measured short completion. Reproducibility determines whether the difference from the 150-ul result should motivate an amount interaction or remain unexplained variability.

m99 at 1/1 and 100 ul is predicted to finish later than the selected 2/1 point despite stronger eluent. Its measured pure-EA condition is compact. This tests a completion peak in a hydroxyester with a fixed large DCM plug.

Pair m99 at 2/1 and 100 ul with its selected 1/1 point to isolate the ratio response at unchanged loading. A measured 150-ul 2/1 reference adds amount context. The pair tests whether the predicted completion peak is supported.

m61 at 1/1 and 50 ul locates where its onset-associated amount differences begin. Higher amounts have similar measured 1/1 onset, whereas the recent low-loading 10/1 experiment began substantially later than its 100-ul counterpart.

Measure m67 at 2/1 and 100 ul alongside the selected 5/1 point. The model predicts both endpoints slightly later at 2/1. This tests whether a nonmonotone feature resembling the recently challenged hydrophobic peaks also occurs in this alcohol.

This m67 5/1 point and its selected 2/1 counterpart connect to measured 10/1 behavior at the same 100-ul loading. A measured 150-ul 5/1 reference helps distinguish ratio curvature from amount dependence.
Pure-EA m212 at 100 ul anchors the strong-eluent end of a secondary amine whose measured 5/1 and 10/1 conditions are much later. Its label tests the predicted contraction of both endpoints.

m212 at 1/1 and 100 ul forms a fixed-loading ratio contrast with the selected pure-EA experiment. A measured 150-ul 1/1 reference supplies amount context. This constrains how the amine's delayed response begins.

Pair this 50-ul m212 1/1 point with the selected 100-ul point. Measured 5/1 records differ greatly across these amounts. This tests whether that association already exists under stronger eluent or remains localized.

Measure tertiary-amino acrylate m19 in pure EA at 100 ul. Its measured 2/1 condition is appreciably retained, while this forecast is compact. This adds an aliphatic-basic anchor without assuming transfer of the aromatic-nitrogen response.

m89 at 50/1 and 150 ul extends its matched-amount curve beyond measured 20/1 conditions. Large measured endpoints at 100 ul and 50/1 motivate testing how the delayed aminoester regime transfers across amount.

The m215 pure-EA forecast is substantially later than measured 1/1 and 2/1 conditions at the same loading. This tests a remaining anomalous strong-eluent peak after the previous hydrophobic 2/1 probes mostly contradicted delayed forecasts.

Measure biphenyl m210 in pure EA at the same amount and DCM plug size as selected naphthalene m215. Measured low-loading biphenyl already has broad completion in pure EA. This comparison tests scaffold specificity without imposing universally narrow hydrocarbon intervals.

m209 at 10/1 and 150 ul fills the matched-amount gap before measured 20/1 and 50/1 conditions. Comparison with measured 50-ul 10/1 behavior tests where phenolic onset and completion acquire different amount responses.

m192 in pure EA at 150 ul supplies a stronger-eluent anchor for a halogenated aldehyde with measured completion growth from 1/1 through 50/1. It tests whether the modest forecast preserves that scaffold's response at unchanged high loading.

m128 at 10/1 and 100 ul extends its measured 2/1 response at unchanged loading. The model predicts substantial completion growth but little onset change. This tests endpoint-specific transfer within a sulfur-containing aryl ketone environment.

m183 at 20/1 and 100 ul pairs with the selected 50/1 experiment to measure weak-eluent curvature at fixed loading. Measured 10/1 observations at neighboring amounts provide context for distinguishing amount variation from ratio response.

Extend the selected m183 20/1 point to 50/1 at unchanged loading. Related flexible aldehydes have long measured completion at 50/1. This tests whether that behavior transfers to the simpler phenylpropionaldehyde environment.

m118 at 2/1 and 100 ul adds a missing stronger-eluent condition before its unusual measured 10/1 onset/completion combination. The recent 150-ul 5/1 label adds context without making a pure amount comparison.

Pure-EA m204 at 150 ul anchors a primary alcohol with strongly delayed measured 5/1 and 10/1 behavior at matched loading. This constrains how far delayed-alcohol corrections should extend toward strong eluent.
m107 at 1/1 and 150 ul precedes measured 2/1 and 5/1 conditions at the same loading. It locates the strong-eluent contraction of this ether-bearing beta-ketoester's long completion response.

m20 at 5/1 and 100 ul fills an ether-acrylate response gap before measured 10/1 behavior. Paired with the selected phenoxyethyl acrylate condition, it tests how ether environment and recorded loading conditions modify the intermediate-strength response.

Measure m21 at 5/1 and 100 ul alongside m20 at the same ratio and sample volume, retaining their different densities and loading solvents explicitly. Existing stronger- and weaker-eluent observations leave a consequential ratio gap.

m74 at 50/1 and 100 ul connects measured 100-ul 10/1 behavior with a 150-ul 50/1 reference. This tests amount transfer in bromomalonate, whose delayed completion contrasts with measured compact unsubstituted malonate behavior.

Measure pentafluorobenzene m156 at 20/1 and 100 ul between measured 10/1 and 50/1 conditions that use different amounts. This supplies a donor-free completion-growth control and tests whether its broad interval develops smoothly.

m62 at 20/1 and 100 ul explores the missing response between compact 2/1 and later 50/1 observations, acknowledging their different amounts. The crowded boronate environment adds conditional information poorly represented by carbonyl analogies.

m202 at 2/1 and 150 ul tests the predicted retention peak between measured pure-EA and 10/1 conditions at the same amount. It helps localize the very different measured 100-ul 10/1 regime without assuming its mechanism.

hypotheses.content: m125 has a substantial, ratio-dependent association between DCM plug volume and completion. Its recurrence at 1/1 and 2/1 does not establish a universal plug effect or guarantee persistence in pure EA.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor barely distinguishes the selected pure-EA plug conditions. Labels can teach scaffold-by-eluent-by-loading interactions instead of averaging substantially different completion regimes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 300-versus-500-ul completion association persist in pure EA, and does its size depend on sample amount?

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading amount is not yet established as the dominant reproducible explanation for large endpoint shifts. Some local amount associations are coherent, but identical-condition differences prevent a general deterministic interpretation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Recorded-feature interactions should be learned locally, while unexplained variation should not become a universal amount correction. The targeted repeat tests the reproducibility of an influential short-completion result.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do missing m92 and m72 amount points form coherent responses, does m81 reproduce its short completion, and does m202 retain a ratio peak at fixed high amount?

hypotheses.content: Alcohol onset requires joint structural, amount, and eluent context. Higher-loading m61's early onset does not transfer automatically to low-loading m61 or related alcohols, while completion may change much less than onset.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This prevents a scaffold-specific onset correction from becoming a generic OH effect. The selected alcohol and hydroxyester curves also test apparent ratio peaks at controlled loading.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At what solvent strength does m61's amount association emerge, and are the predicted m67 onset peak and m99 completion peak supported by fixed-loading pairs?

hypotheses.content: The delayed 2/1 predictions were overgeneralized across recently tested hydrophobic compounds. Compact retention remains a useful local prior, with the extreme low-loading m133 observation an unresolved counterexample and broad completion still possible in donor-free aromatics.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Suspicious ratio peaks can affect common rows even when quantile spreads are modest. Pure-EA comparisons test another such feature while preserving legitimate scaffold-specific completion differences.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does naphthalene elute later in pure EA than at 1/1 and 2/1, and does matched-loading biphenyl support a shared or localized response?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing molecules need structure-specific eluent-response curves and stronger-eluent anchors. Aromatic nitrogen, aminoesters, and aliphatic amines should not inherit a common delayed-retention correction across all ratios and amounts.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Recent quinoline anchors support ordinary stronger-eluent regimes despite large historical weak-eluent failures. Extending that constraint to distinct amine environments can improve conditional transfer.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m212 and m19 become compact in pure EA, does m212's amount association persist at 1/1, and does m89's delayed 50/1 response transfer to 150 ul?

hypotheses.content: Onset and completion have distinct structure-dependent response curves. Long completion can coexist with early onset, while other scaffolds develop delayed onset at weaker eluent; donor counts and broad carbonyl categories do not determine the transition.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Separate endpoint learning can repair completion errors without imposing delayed onset on every related row. Selected aldehyde, sulfur-containing ketone, phenol, and donor-free aromatic conditions test different parts of these curves.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do missing aldehyde and ketone conditions show gradual completion growth or separate onset transitions, and how do m209 and m156 constrain transfer across functional-group environments?

hypotheses.content: Measured ester and ether-containing families span very different retention responses. Local functional-group environment together with recorded conditions is likely more informative than acceptor counts alone, although present comparisons do not isolate a single causal structural feature.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Compact malonate, delayed beta-ketoester, and ether-acrylate examples can otherwise be conflated by broad polarity features. Intermediate-ratio and matched-amount labels constrain structural interactions among these rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m20 and m21 differ at 5/1 as forecast, and do the new m107 and m74 points preserve their distinct stronger- and weaker-eluent responses?

feedback_interpretation: Latest m125 outcomes strengthen a specific plug-volume association: at 1/1, both 100- and 150-ul samples finish near 38–39 mL with 500-ul plugs, versus about 20 mL with 300-ul plugs. The new m72 package contrast is small, so the package hypothesis should remain scaffold-specific. Low-loading m61 measured 11.11/15.86 mL, weakening the proposed persistence of very early onset across amounts and strengthening endpoint-specific condition modeling. The hydrophobic 2/1 probes mostly rejected delayed forecasts, redirecting attention to remaining suspicious condition peaks. The m208 outcome confirms that weak-eluent phenolic responses can still be badly underestimated, while related phenol and beta-diketone outcomes argue against a universal tail correction. The m194 pure-EA series supports a local completion increase at 150 ul, but conflicting identical-condition observations elsewhere still weaken a general loading law. The supplied recent feedback attributes one outcome to m92 whereas the observed table assigns that record to m142. I use observed-table attribution; m92 at 1/1, 150 ul with EA loading remains an unmeasured condition in that table.
batch_rationale: The batch focuses on relationships retraining can learn from the catalog's recorded inputs. Three m125 experiments test transfer of a strengthened plug association. Missing m92 and m72 amount points and one m81 repeat distinguish useful loading relationships from unexplained variation. Fixed-loading alcohol, hydroxyester, aldehyde, and amine contrasts test response curvature and separate onset changes from completion changes. Strong-eluent anchors constrain the spread of delayed-retention corrections, while the naphthalene/biphenyl comparison targets a suspicious prediction in common hydrophobic chemistry. Ester/ether conditions and the boronate point extend conditional coverage where broad polarity descriptors offer weak guidance. Multiple points on a molecule serve explicit comparisons; other choices fill consequential gaps. This may improve overall Row-distribution accuracy through better structure-condition interactions and distinct V1/V2 responses, without selecting for maximal elution volume or treating interval width as uncertainty.
